newsitem.title: USA: North American bunkers higher, but talk is subdued.
newsitem.headline: North American bunkers higher, but talk is subdued.

text.p: North American bunker prices were mostly higher on Thursday though action was mostly amid views one players in Houston may be holding back barrels in in an effort to stoke prices a bit higher, traders said.
Most of the action was concentrated in Houston, with East and West Coast markets considerably quieter and generally harder to call.

A deal for 380 CST was heard done in Houston earlier in the day at $92.50 a tonne, but by the end of the day, offers were up to $95. Some traders foresee the Houston 380 CST market soon crossing the $100 threshold.
Houston 180 CST was pegged a touch higher at between $96 and $98 a tonne.
In New York, 380 was talked as high as $104 to $105 a tonne as the Houston-New York spread returned to more typical levels. The 180 CST market was heard offered as high as $110 a tonne, traders said.
On the West Coast, 180 CST was heard done in Los Angeles in the early going at $94, but that deal was said to be below market, with broader prices heard at around $99.
The upside move in bunker markets was seen capped by the bearishness on NYMEX, where crude has slipped down all year.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
